projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: A sustained count of 20+ connected devices, a recent spike to 27, and zero camera motion for over four hours strongly suggests the house is either unoccupied or the family is confined to a camera-blind zone. Given the active dogs and typical Sunday morning routine, this prolonged lack of movement is highly unusual and warrants a quick check-in to ensure everyone is safe.

The sudden drop in connected devices to 20, followed by a stable count and zero camera motion over four hours, strongly indicates the household is currently away or in a prolonged 'away' mode, with the remaining devices likely being stationary IoT infrastructure. This confirms the home is unoccupied, suggesting it's safe to activate security and energy-saving routines.

The rapid drop in connected devices (24 to 20) between 08:46 and 08:48, paired with zero camera motion, indicates family members likely departed via a camera-blind exit or disabled Wi-Fi rather than using monitored areas. This suggests a potential security blind spot or a change in the weekend morning routine worth noting.

The persistent presence count of 23-29 combined with zero camera motion over four hours indicates the system is likely counting IoT/smart home devices rather than people, which may trigger false occupancy automations. This aligns with a quiet Sunday morning where the family is probably still asleep or in private areas.
The connected device count dropped rapidly from ~29 to ~23 between 07:14 and 07:27, strongly indicating the household is departing the home, likely for a Sunday morning outing.

The sustained 28-30 connected devices and zero camera activity are confirmed benign: both adults report ~9+ hours of sleep with stable vitals, indicating the household is in a normal deep sleep state with devices left charging or connected in bedrooms and common areas.

The sustained presence of 29-30 connected devices from 22:28 onward, combined with zero camera activity, strongly indicates a large group of guests is already settled inside the house. This quiet, high-occupancy state past midnight suggests a late gathering rather than an intrusion, but a quick perimeter check may be prudent.

The sudden spike to 29 connected devices at 22:28, with no corresponding camera activity, suggests either unexpected guests just connected their phones inside or a network/IoT surge; worth a quick check to confirm who is on the premises.

The stable count of 22 devices likely reflects static IoT hardware rather than active people, and combined with zero camera motion over a four-hour Saturday afternoon, strongly suggests either a prolonged stationary activity or a camera system offline state; verifying camera status is recommended.

The device count stabilized at 22 for four hours with zero camera activity, confirming a sustained absence since ~11:15 AM rather than a temporary outing or network glitch. This pattern indicates a planned departure, so verify security arming and confirm pet status if any trackers were among the dropped devices.
